svg.text: A SAR collection samples k-space on a POLAR grid. The 2-D FFT needs a uniform RECTANGULAR one. Stages 1-2 get from
the left picture to the right, and the MIDDLE picture is what the range interpolation alone produces.
1 COLLECTED -- polar
2 after RANGE resample
3 after AZIMUTH resample
kr[i,j] = 2 pr[i]/c (f0[i] + j df[i])
Each pulse i is an arc at its own aspect
angle; j steps outward in range frequency.
x0 and dx differ pulse to pulse, so the arcs
are neither concentric in index nor evenly spaced.
t = (KR[q] - x0_i)/dx_i, k = floor(t), mu = t-k
COLUMNS now line up: every pulse has been
resampled onto the SAME kx grid. Rows do not,
because each pulse was only made uniform along
its OWN radial. Hence a second resample.
u = KC[q]/kr, k from a merge scan on tan(phi)
Uniform in BOTH axes, so a separable 2-D FFT
applies and the hardware runs two 1-D passes with
a transpose between. That transpose is the
corner-turn.
